title: 36.7 A 1.54pJ/b 64Gb/s 16-QAM Intradyne Coherent Optical Receiver in 28nm CMOS
problem: Short-reach optical links require higher data rates than noncoherent formats (OOK, PAM-4) can achieve; coherent detection with 16-QAM modulation doubles throughput but demands high-linearity analog signal processing and carrier phase recovery while maintaining low power consumption.
motivation: Data center bandwidth demands drive scaling beyond legacy noncoherent links; coherent optical receivers enable higher spectral efficiency but face challenges in low-power integration.
method: The receiver uses an analog phase detector—a circuit that measures the timing offset between the incoming optical signal and an internal reference light source (running at the same frequency on the chip)—to keep them synchronized. Instead of using power-hungry digital processing to recover the carrier phase (synchronize to the incoming signal's exact timing), this analog circuit does it with simple electronics. The design decodes 16-QAM signals (which encode information in 16 distinct signal states) at 64 gigabits per second.
key_novelty: An analog phase detector that synchronizes the receiver's internal light source with the incoming signal enables 16-QAM decoding at 1.54 picojoules per bit without requiring high-power digital processing.
contributions: First 16-QAM intradyne coherent receiver in 28nm CMOS
Novel analog phase detector for robust CPR
Low-complexity alternative to DSP-heavy coherent receivers
